item.title: U2 Is Taking It To The Streets Of Mexico City For New Music Video: Watch
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome back to "Trending on Billboard". Today, we've got some exciting news about one of the world's most iconic rock bands, U2. The Irish legends are back, and this time, they're hitting the streets of Mexico City to shoot a new music video.
[Short music clip: U2]
Host: Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton, and Larry Mullen Jr. were spotted in the Mexican capital, rocking out on top of a school bus, graffitied by local artist Chavis Mármol. The new track, "Street of Dreams", is part of their upcoming studio album, due out later this year.
Host: This isn't the first time U2 has brought the streets to a standstill. Who can forget their famous rooftop performance in downtown Los Angeles back in the late '80s? The footage from that performance was used in their Grammy Award-winning music video for "Where the Streets Have No Name".
[Short music clip: "Where the Streets Have No Name"]
Host: But that's not all that's happening in Mexico City this week. The city is also hosting the 2026 Street Child World Cup, with 30 teams from around the globe participating. U2 drummer Larry Mullen Jr. had this to say about the event: "It's a little NGO with a big kick for kids with all of the talent and none of the access. Our band are proud supporters."
Host: U2's next album is the follow-up to 2023's "Songs of Surrender", which debuted at number 5 on the Billboard 200 chart. The band has been active lately, with the release of their Easter Lily EP in April. Bono shared an update on the new album, saying they're working towards a "noisy, messy, 'unreasonably colourful' album" to play live.
[Outro music starts]
Host: That's all for today. U2 is certainly making waves, and we can't wait to hear more from their upcoming album. With 34 songs on the Billboard Hot 100, including two number one hits, and eight number one albums on the Billboard 200 chart, U2 continues to be one of the most iconic and influential bands of our time.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
